original_question: When, if ever, will Facebook contain more profiles of dead people than of living ones?
short_answer_summary: Source-era demographic projections suggest the2060s if Facebook declines or the2130s/mid2100s if it persists.
detailed_scientific_explanation: Facebook’s initially young population means few deceased users relative to living ones. Combining growth history and age distribution suggests10–20million deceased account creators by the source date.

As early cohorts age, annual deaths rise even if registration stops. The decisive variable is new young-user adoption. A decline beginning later in the2010s gives crossover around2065; a long-lasting infrastructure-like service could postpone it to the mid2100s.

Projections assume accounts are not deleted and partly extrapolate US age/use and mortality data globally. Different adoption histories shift landmarks; mass deletion or sudden mortality changes could overturn them.

Dead accounts create relatively little new data, so indefinite retention may be inexpensive. The closing discussion concerns access, privacy, memorialization and new social norms for mourning rather than merely storage.
initial_assumptions: Some US demographic data extrapolated worldwide.

quantitative_facts.detail: About290,000 US Facebook users died2013;worldwide severalmillion;annual deaths expected double in7years and again7years later.
Persistent-service crossover as late as mid2100s; opening answer says2130s.
